title: Checks for assert statements that use a string literal as the first argument.
summary: An assert on a non-empty string literal will always pass, while an assert on an empty string literal will always fail. Ruff takes this rule from Pylint and made it stable in v0.0.258.
message_templates: Asserting on an empty string literal will never pass
Asserting on a non-empty string literal will always pass
Asserting on a string literal may have unintended results

title: Checks for uses of named expressions (e.g., a := 42) that can be replaced by regular assignment statements (e.g., a = 42).
summary: While a top-level named expression is syntactically and semantically valid, it's less clear than a regular assignment statement. Named expressions are intended to be used in comprehensions and generator expressions, where assignment statements are not allowed. Ruff takes this rule from Pylint and made it stable in v0.0.270.
message_templates: Named expression used without context

title: Checks for an exception that is not raised.
summary: It's unnecessary to create an exception without raising it. For example, ValueError("...") on its own will have no effect (unlike raise ValueError("...")) and is likely a mistake. Ruff takes this rule from Pylint and made it stable in 0.5.0.
message_templates: Missing `raise` statement on exception

title: Checks for comparisons against NaN values.
summary: Comparing against a NaN value can lead to unexpected results. For example, float("NaN") == float("NaN") will return False and, in general, x == float("NaN") will always return False, even if x is NaN. Ruff takes this rule from Pylint and made it stable in 0.12.0.
message_templates: Comparing against a NaN value; use `math.isnan` instead
Comparing against a NaN value; use `np.isnan` instead

title: Checks for static methods that use self or cls as their first argument.
summary: This rule also applies to __new__ methods, which are implicitly static. PEP 8 recommends the use of self and cls as the first arguments for instance methods and class methods, respectively. Naming the first argument of a static method as self or cls can be misleading, as static methods do not receive an instance or class reference as their first argument. Ruff takes this rule from Pylint and made it stable in 0.6.0.
message_templates: First argument of a static method should not be named `{}`

title: Checks for a re-defined slot in a subclass.
summary: If a class defines a slot also defined in a base class, the instance variable defined by the base class slot is inaccessible (except by retrieving its descriptor directly from the base class). Ruff takes this rule from Pylint. It is in preview.
message_templates: Slot `{}` redefined from base class `{}`

title: Detects attempts to use super without parentheses.
summary: The super() callable can be used inside method definitions to create a proxy object that delegates attribute access to a superclass of the current class. Attempting to access attributes on super itself, however, instead of the object returned by a call to super(), will raise AttributeError. Ruff takes this rule from Pylint and made it stable in 0.5.0.
message_templates: `super` call is missing parentheses

title: Checks for import statements that import the current module.
summary: Importing a module from itself is a circular dependency and results in an ImportError exception. Ruff takes this rule from Pylint and made it stable in v0.0.265.
message_templates: Module `{}` imports itself

title: Checks for global variables that are not assigned a value in the current scope.
summary: The global keyword allows an inner scope to modify a variable declared in the outer scope. If the variable is not modified within the inner scope, there is no need to use global. Ruff takes this rule from Pylint and made it stable in v0.0.174.
message_templates: Using global for `{}` but no assignment is done

title: Checks for the use of global statements to update identifiers.
summary: Pylint discourages the use of global variables as global mutable state is a common source of bugs and confusing behavior. Ruff takes this rule from Pylint and made it stable in v0.0.253.
message_templates: Using the global statement to update `{}` is discouraged

title: Checks for uses of the global keyword at the module level.
summary: The global keyword is used within functions to indicate that a name refers to a global variable, rather than a local variable. Ruff takes this rule from Pylint and made it stable in 0.5.0.
message_templates: `global` at module level is redundant

title: Checks for assignment of self and cls in instance and class methods respectively.
summary: The identifiers self and cls are conventional in Python for the first parameter of instance methods and class methods, respectively. Assigning new values to these variables can be confusing for others reading your code; using a different variable name can lead to clearer code. Ruff takes this rule from Pylint and made it stable in 0.6.0.
message_templates: Reassigned `{}` variable in {} method

title: Checks for except clauses that attempt to catch multiple exceptions with a binary operation (and or or).
summary: A binary operation will not catch multiple exceptions. Instead, the binary operation will be evaluated first, and the result of _that_ operation will be caught (for an or operation, this is typically the first exception in the list). This is almost never the desired behavior. Ruff takes this rule from Pylint and made it stable in v0.0.258.
message_templates: Exception to catch is the result of a binary `and` operation
Exception to catch is the result of a binary `or` operation

title: Checks for try clauses with too many statements.
summary: Try clauses with many statements make unexpected exceptions harder to detect and debug. Ruff takes this rule from Pylint. It is in preview.
message_templates: Try clause contains too many statements ({} > {})

title: Check for an invalid mode argument in open calls.
summary: The open function accepts a mode argument that specifies how the file should be opened (e.g., read-only, write-only, append-only, etc.). Ruff takes this rule from Pylint and made it stable in 0.5.0.
message_templates: `{}` is not a valid mode for `open`

title: Check for shallow os.environ copies.
summary: os.environ is not a dict object, but rather, a proxy object. As such, mutating a shallow copy of os.environ will also mutate the original object. Ruff takes this rule from Pylint and made it stable in 0.10.0.
message_templates: Shallow copy of `os.environ` via `copy.copy(os.environ)`

title: Checks for os.getenv calls with invalid default values.
summary: If an environment variable is set, os.getenv will return its value as a string. If the environment variable is _not_ set, os.getenv will return None, or the default value if one is provided. Ruff takes this rule from Pylint and made it stable in v0.0.255.
message_templates: Invalid type for environment variable default; expected `str` or `None`

title: Checks for uses of subprocess.Popen with a preexec_fn argument.
summary: The preexec_fn argument is unsafe within threads as it can lead to deadlocks. Furthermore, preexec_fn is targeted for deprecation. Ruff takes this rule from Pylint and made it stable in v0.0.281.
message_templates: `preexec_fn` argument is unsafe when using threads

title: Checks for uses of subprocess.run without an explicit check argument.
summary: By default, subprocess.run does not check the return code of the process it runs. This can lead to silent failures. Ruff takes this rule from Pylint and made it stable in v0.0.285.
message_templates: `subprocess.run` without explicit `check` argument

title: Checks for uses of open and related calls without an explicit encoding argument.
summary: Using open in text mode without an explicit encoding can lead to non-portable code, with differing behavior across platforms. While readers may assume that UTF-8 is the default encoding, in reality, the default is locale-specific. Ruff takes this rule from Pylint. It is in preview.
message_templates: `{}` in text mode without explicit `encoding` argument
`{}` without explicit `encoding` argument

title: Checks for classes that implement __eq__ but not __hash__.
summary: A class that implements __eq__ but not __hash__ will have its hash method implicitly set to None, regardless of if a superclass defines __hash__. This will cause the class to be unhashable, which will in turn cause issues when using instances of the class as keys in a dictionary or members of a set. Ruff takes this rule from Pylint and made it stable in 0.12.0.
message_templates: Object does not implement `__hash__` method

title: Checks for lock objects that are created and immediately discarded in with statements.
summary: Creating a lock (via threading.Lock or similar) in a with statement has no effect, as locks are only relevant when shared between threads. Ruff takes this rule from Pylint and made it stable in 0.5.0.
message_templates: Threading lock directly created in `with` statement has no effect

title: Checks for variables defined in for loops and with statements that get overwritten within the body, for example by another for loop or with statement or by direct assignment.
summary: Redefinition of a loop variable inside the loop's body causes its value to differ from the original loop iteration for the remainder of the block, in a way that will likely cause bugs. Ruff takes this rule from Pylint and made it stable in v0.0.252.
message_templates: Outer {} variable `{}` overwritten by inner {} target
{} variable `{}` overwritten by {} target

title: Checks for dunder methods that have no special meaning in Python 3.
summary: Misspelled or no longer supported dunder name methods may cause your code to not function as expected. Ruff takes this rule from Pylint. It is in preview.
message_templates: Dunder method `{}` has no special meaning in Python 3

title: Checks for nested min and max calls.
summary: Nested min and max calls can be flattened into a single call to improve readability. Ruff takes this rule from Pylint and made it stable in v0.0.266.
message_templates: Nested `{}` calls can be flattened
